---
title: "Estimate transitions"
description: "Fit adjacent-cycle probabilities, baseline entry outcomes and ordered within-cycle stages."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis)
invisible(capture.output(source(system.file(
  "examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"
), local = TRUE)))
```

Choose the estimator according to what the observations represent.

| Question | Function |
|:--|:--|
| What label follows the current complete cycle? | `estimateTransitions()` |
| What is the first label after an explicitly defined baseline? | `estimateEntryTransitions()` |
| What happens in each analyst-defined stage within a cycle? | `estimateStageTransitions()` |

The snippets use the synthetic [quickstart data](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/quickstart.R).
Run this first in your own session:

```{r load-example, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"))
```

## Fit adjacent-cycle probabilities

```{r fit-adjacent}
transitions <- estimateTransitions(histories)
transitionMatrix(transitions)
```

A pair qualifies when the source is a complete cycle and its immediately
adjacent destination has a known label. A short final destination can qualify.
Gaps, unresolved labels and administrative exits never imply transitions. A
last label without a successor does not imply a self-transition.

Denominators count eligible outgoing pairs. Inspect `transitions$estimates`
for counts and denominators; stratified fits also report patient support.
Unsupported nonabsorbing rows remain `NA`;
declared absorbing rows are structural identities. Missing support is not
replaced by pooled probabilities.

## Separate follow-up periods

```{r fit-periods}
period_fit <- estimateTransitions(
  histories, periodBreaks = c(0, 7, Inf),
  periodLabels = c("First week", "Later")
)
transitionMatrix(period_fit, period = "First week")
```

Periods use days from each patient's index date. Boundaries start at zero,
end at `Inf` and align with the cycle length. Lower boundaries are included;
upper boundaries are excluded. A pair belongs to its **source** period even
when the destination falls in the next one.

## Fit covariate-specific models

```{r fit-strata}
rows <- trajectories
rows$age <- ifelse(rows$subject_id %in% c("p1", "p3"), 64, 70)
groups <- list(age_group = list(
  column = "age", breaks = c(0, 65, Inf), labels = c("Under 65", "65+")
))
rows <- addCovariateGroups(rows, groups)
grouped <- prepareTrajectories(rows, cycleLength = 7, absorbingStates = "Dead")
group_fit <- estimateTransitions(grouped, strata = "age_group")
group_fit$strata
transitionMatrix(group_fit, stratum = group_fit$strata$stratum_id[1])
```

Each source row's complete covariate combination selects its group. Covariates
may change between cycles; transitions across groups are retained. Numeric
values make exact-value groups unless you create bands first. Use the returned
registry to interpret `stratum_id`; it is not a covariate value. Supporting
patient counts cannot be added across groups or periods.

## Estimate baseline-to-first-label entry

```{r fit-entry}
entry <- estimateEntryTransitions(histories, entryState = "Stable")
entry$coverage
entry$matrix
```

`entryState` is a supplied clinical baseline, not an inferred earlier state.
Alternatively, supply one row per patient with `subject_id` and `entry_state`.
For stratified entry, include baseline covariates in that table and name them
in `strata`. Later trajectory values are not substituted for missing baseline
information.

A known complete first cycle qualifies, as does a short first cycle ending in
a declared absorbing state. Exclusions appear in `entry$subjects`. Probabilities
and the default baseline mix use eligible patients only, without censoring
adjustment. A first-cycle death in ordinary `entryCounts` remains a first label;
it does not create an assumed preceding alive-to-death transition.

## Model ordered events within a cycle

For onset followed by mortality, supply one evaluable outcome per stage:

```{r fit-stages}
observations <- data.frame(
  subject_id = rep(c("p1", "p2"), each = 2), source_day = 0,
  stage = rep(c("onset", "mortality"), 2),
  from_state = c("Stable", "Complication", "Stable", "Stable"),
  to_state = c("Complication", "Dead", "Stable", "Stable"), observed = TRUE
)
stage_fit <- estimateStageTransitions(
  observations, stageOrder = c("onset", "mortality"), definition = histories,
  identityStates = list(onset = "Complication")
)
transitionMatrix(stage_fit, stage = "onset")
```

`observed = FALSE` excludes an unevaluable outcome from its stage denominator.
`identityStates` declares unchanged rows for a stage; unsupported rows otherwise
remain unknown. Stages add no elapsed time.

`prepareStageObservations()` can build these rows from aligned C2T views in
stage order, with an explicit first-cycle `entryState`. Matching patient-cycle
boundaries are required. Complete final cycles qualify by default; short final
cycles qualify with an absorbing final outcome. `requireNextCycle = TRUE`
requires another observed cycle for nonabsorbing outcomes. See the
[C2T-to-ICER example](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/c2t-to-icer.R).
For supplied stage matrices, use `composeTransitionStages()` instead.
